review_model_policy.name: glm-tiered-astra-final-v3
review_model_policy.description: Every exact head is triaged by gpt-6-astra (low effort) into trivial/low/normal/critical; the tier sets the reviewer --effort per phase. Phase-1 glm-5.3-flash reviewers (general plus every selected specialist) run at the tier's phase1 effort and a fresh distinct gpt-5.6-sol gate verifier validates them. A zero-blocker gate admits Phase-2 gpt-6-astra reviewers at the tier's phase2 effort and a fresh distinct gpt-6-astra final verifier (fixed high); a trivial tier with zero blockers publishes the final review from Phase 1 alone and discloses the skip. Blockers always take precedence over tier. Missing, failed, stale-head, wrong-model, reused, or unparseable evidence fails closed. Persisted codex/sonnet keys remain compatibility aliases only.

triage.label: complexity-triage

trivial.meaning: typo/docs/rename/format/config-only, no behaviour change; Phase 2 skipped

critical.meaning: large/complex, or consensus/funds/crypto/security/storage where a bug is critical; never above xhigh

triage.rule: effort per phase = tiers[tier]; verifiers keep their fixed reasoning; blockers found in Phase 1 always publish preliminary regardless of tier

reviewer.label: phase1-glm-flash
reviewer.effort_note: default; the triage tier overrides --effort per run and the value used is persisted per lane

reviewer.label: phase2-astra
reviewer.effort_note: default; the triage tier overrides --effort per run and the value used is persisted per lane

preliminary.title: Preliminary review — Phase 1 blocker gate
preliminary.phase2: Phase 2 (gpt-6-astra) not run (deferred by blocker gate)

final_phase1_only.title: Final review — Phase 1 only ({tier} change)
final_phase1_only.phase2: not run (triage rated this change trivial)
final_phase1_only.event: COMMENT (never APPROVE: Phase 2 did not run)

review_model_policy.checkpoint_migration: same-head policy identity or fingerprint mismatch restarts Phase 1; mismatched evidence cannot resume or satisfy policy v3
review_model_policy.provenance_rule: Persist exact policy identity/fingerprint, head, phase, decision, canonical blocker count, reviewer/verifier attempt IDs, logical agents, exact backend models, per-lane --effort and the triage tier/model/reasoning, harness/auth/roles/read-only launch contract, PIDs, exit statuses, artifacts, status/parseability, prior-finding revalidation, deterministic policy result, coverage, publication IDs, and every verifier attempt.

specialists.description: Deep security analysis: cryptographic implementations, consensus safety, proof system soundness, race conditions in concurrent code, web/DOM injection, remote dependency boundaries, trust boundary violations, unsafe operations, timing attacks

Rust quality review: error handling discipline (no unwraps in production), architectural patterns, idiomatic Rust usage, proper lifetimes/generics, test structure, performance patterns (unnecessary clones, allocation in hot paths)
FFI and cross-language boundary review: memory safety across Swift/Rust/WASM boundaries, correct ownership transfer, FFI-safe types, panic safety across FFI, WASM binding correctness, ABI stability

Bitcoin Core backport prerequisite verification: compares upstream starting states vs Dash to detect missing intermediate PRs, identifies workarounds masking missing APIs/infrastructure, traces dependency chains. Activated for PRs with 'backport' in title or cherry-picks from bitcoin/bitcoin.

TenderDash (Go) consensus and security review: BFT protocol correctness (propose/prevote/precommit, locking, +2/3 thresholds, double-sign / equivocation), validator set + LLMQ quorum signature verification (BLS threshold sigs, quorum hash binding, chain-id and domain separation), vote/commit/block/header validation, evidence handling, light client safety, ABCI app-vs-consensus trust boundary, RPC and P2P input validation, DoS / resource exhaustion (unbounded allocations, slow peers, mempool flooding), Go concurrency (data races, deadlocks, goroutine leaks), nondeterminism in consensus-critical paths.

Dash Core commit-history hygiene review (no code correctness). Dashpay/dash merges PR commits into develop without squashing, so the ordered stack lands in permanent history. Flags fixup/wip/no-op commits, obviously separate commits that should be squashed, misleading commit messages, mixed unrelated changes in a single commit visible from per-commit stats, and merge/rebase noise — while leaving legitimate multi-commit stacks (refactor+feature+tests, backport/cherry-pick series, justified mechanical follow-ups) alone.
